lines: One email, one code, never a password: that's how Telo Ride knows it's you.
Type your email and choose Send my code. Until the backend answers, the button reads Sending your code, and waits.
An address that isn't one sends nothing. The field is marked, and the error under it is read out.
Then the code screen names the address the code went to, and Send a new code counts down thirty seconds.
The backend answers the same whether or not you have an account, keeps only a keyed hash of the code, and emails it over SMTP.
Codes are limited: five an hour for an address, twenty for a network. Ask too often, and the screen says when to try again.
From a phone to a desktop, sign-in is one calm panel.
What the tests prove: the code goes to the address as you typed it, a bad address goes nowhere, and every limit answers with when to come back.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
